 Between Shenandoah National Park And Gettysburg Is Virginia's Town With Boutique Shops And Mountain Trails
 By   Audrey Simons 
 Oct. 24, 2026 1:45 pm EST 
 Volodymyr Sadovyy/Google Maps 
 Add Islands on Google: 
 Preferred Source 
 Google Discover 
 The Shenandoah Valley stretches between the Blue Ridge Mountains and the Allegheny Mountains, primarily through Western Virginia. The sweeping corridor is blanketed by beautiful rolling pastures and scattered woodlands, along with a bevy of bucolic small towns. Berryville could easily serve as the poster child for the region, lying out in the countryside on the valley's north end, about 60 miles outside of Washington, D.C. Like many Virginia towns, Berryville's roots stretch back to the colonial era. The Clarke County community was established in the 1770s, when it was known as Battletown. 
 The town's original name may sound like a nod to the American Revolutionary War, but according to local lore , the town apparently earned its moniker for the frequent fistfights that broke out at the neighborhood tavern. Don't worry, though — present-day Berryville is a much friendlier place. As one local shared on Niche , it's "a cute little town reminiscent of 50s America," where "everyone knows everyone and respects each other." The community stands at the junction of U.S. Route 340 and State Route 7, near the winding Shenandoah River. The town is only about a 35-minute drive from the Washington Dulles International Airport (IAD), with no traffic. 
 Positioned in between Gettysburg, Pennsylvania, and Shenandoah National Park, one of the U.S.' most accessible national parks , Berryville is close enough to major cities and recreation areas to make it a great day trip or weekend getaway. Take in all the historic landmarks as you peruse the boutiques in downtown Berryville, or venture out to one of the surrounding mountain trails for an adventurous trek.
 Old-world vibes and bespoke finds in Berryville, Virginia
 Timothy Vincent/Google Maps 
 Like many of America's most charming and walkable downtowns , Berryville's commercial core is centered around an old-world Main Street. Stretching for several blocks in the heart of town, Berryville's historic downtown district is still lined with vintage buildings, some of which date as far back as the late 1700s. Check out all the classic architecture as you pop into some of the local shops. There are shelves full of unique gifts at  Modern Mercantile , one of the more popular shopping spots in town. Sift through the bespoke jewelry pieces, browse the charming household accents, or pick up something for your pet. "Best little shop in town," one Google reviewer shared, adding that the place is "wonderfully curated" so you can "find something for everyone on your list."
 Head across the street to the  Coiner Grand Emporium . The old-fashioned bazaar originally opened its doors as a department store in the late 1800s. Today, there is an eclectic mix of new and vintage merchandise, along with a variety of Civil War prints and paintings. Venture down Main Street to Hip and Humble Interiors and browse the selection of salvaged building supplies, antique furniture, and other home pieces. "The shop is beautifully curated," a shopper wrote on Yelp . "Every corner feels inspiring and it's definitely worth the trip if you love design, vintage, or just discovering something special."
 Roam the mountains around Berryville, Virginia
 Jon Bilous/Getty Images 
 The Blue Ridge and Allegheny Mountains are among the prettiest subranges of the sprawling Appalachian Mountains system. The Allegheny Mountains stretch across West Virginia to the west of Berryville, while the Blue Ridge Mountains hug the town to the east. Needless to say, Berryville is primely positioned for outdoor adventures. In terms of rugged treks, it doesn't get any more iconic than the nearly 2,200-mile-long Appalachian National Scenic Trail, located just minutes from town. Head a few miles east along State Route 7 toward Bluemont,  a Virginia village known for its peaceful trails and picturesque vineyard , and you'll find several access points to the popular trail.
 If you're up for a challenge, set out from the Raven Rocks Trailhead off Pine Grove Road. Dubbed " the roller-coaster " by locals, this 5-mile rocky route will take you just across state lines toward Raven Rocks, a nearly 1,500-foot-high peak in West Virginia. "Fun trail. Lovely view at the end," one rambler shared online, recommending sturdy hiking boots. "Entire trail is very 'bumpy' lots of rocks and tree roots. Keep your eyes on the ground the entire time and you'll be fine!"
 For a shorter hike with roughly half as much elevation gain, opt for the Buzzard Hill  segment. The trailhead is off Morgans Mill Road, about 10 miles southeast of Berryville. Stretching for roughly 3.5 miles out-and-back, this wooded route will take you by a scenic waterfall and the ruins of an old cabin. "My 9 year old had no complaints and was able to keep a steady pace," one hiker wrote on AllTrails . "Not a huge amount of other hikers, even on a federal holiday," they added. No matter which path you pick, be sure to read up on all the unwritten rules to follow when hiking the Appalachian Trail , so you know what to expect.
